# KS-1033 - Wednesday's task for Ornith, BASH_PATCH (written 2026-09-16 from the files at develop M55 `48e65c435`: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-demo-mutation.sh` read whole (141 lines), `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/run-code-guards.sh` read whole (225 lines) for the DEFERRED bucket entry, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:637-668` for leg 15, and `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh` read whole for the bare-remote git-fixture shape). ⚠ NOT pre-measured: this commission is READ-ONLY against the Secuura checkout, so no scratch clone was built and no run was executed - every claim below is from reading the tip, and every `-` line was measured byte-for-byte (see the raise notes).

## What is wrong (one paragraph)

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-demo-mutation.sh` refuses any change that touches a demo-shaping path
unless a commit in the range carries `[demo-mutation-allowed]`. It decides the range at `:51-60`: a
`GITHUB_BASE_REF` wins, then an explicit `$1`, and otherwise **it falls back to `BASE="origin/main"`
(`:58`)** and diffs `"$BASE...$HEAD"` (`:69`). The three-dot form takes the merge-base, which is right -
but the merge-base of `origin/main` and any develop-based branch is the point where `develop` was last
merged to `main`, **not** the branch point. Under Git Flow `develop` is permanently ahead of `main`, so
every develop-based branch is shown the whole develop-vs-main delta as if it were its own change. KS-1033
measured that on a branch that touched nothing: the guard reported four demo files as modified
(`deployment/azure/env.demo.json`, `migrate/Dockerfile`, `migrate/init.sql`, `migrate/run-platform.sh`).
This is not an abstract complaint - it is the sole reason the guard is UNWIRED. `run-code-guards.sh:116`
holds it in the `DEFERRED` bucket with exactly this reason and exactly this remedy in its own words:
*"Fix its base to the merge-base with origin/develop before wiring."* Until that is done the guard is a
check that cannot run, which is the defect KS-926 exists for; wired as-is it would demand
`[demo-mutation-allowed]` from every author on every push, which is the `--no-verify` generator KS-926
warns about. Changing the fallback to `origin/develop` makes `"$BASE...$HEAD"` resolve to the branch
point, so the diff contains the branch's own commits and nothing else.

**This is item 1 of KS-1033 and ONLY item 1.** The ticket records three unwired guards. Item 2
(`check-no-trust-header-reads.sh`, whose printed advice contradicts its own default) is explicitly
decision-class - the ticket says *"Deciding which is the point"* - and item 3
(`check-container-isolation.sh`) is a relocation to stack start-up, not an edit. Neither is touched here.
**Nothing in this task wires the guard**, either: it stays in `DEFERRED` and leg 15's census still
accounts for it, because wiring is a separate call that wants a measured push. This task removes the one
measured blocker the ticket names.

## Where

Every line number below is in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-demo-mutation.sh` at the tip.

- `:58` — **the defect.** `  BASE="origin/main"` — the fallback that makes every develop-based branch look
  like it changed the demo. The string `BASE="origin/main"` occurs ONCE in the file, so the hunk's span
  is unique.
- `:50` — **the comment that states the fallback.** `# default to comparing against origin/main.` It must
  move with the code; a comment naming `origin/main` beside code reading `origin/develop` is the next
  reader's trap. Unique in the file.
- `:51` — (correct) `if [ -n "${GITHUB_BASE_REF:-}" ]; then` — the branch that wins ahead of the default.
  Stays exactly as it is; cell 4 is the control that proves it.
- `:52` — (correct) `  BASE="origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}"` stays untouched.
- `:55` — (correct) `  BASE="$1"` — the explicit-argument override. Stays untouched.
- `:69` — (correct) `CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE...$HEAD" 2>/dev/null || true)`. The
  THREE-dot form is already right and is what makes the one-word change sufficient. Stays; do not change
  it to two dots.
- `:63` — (correct) `if ! git rev-parse --verify "$BASE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then` — the guard that prints
  `base $BASE not found; nothing to compare` and exits 0 on a fresh clone. Stays; it is what keeps the
  new default safe on a tree with no `origin/develop`.
- `:44` — (correct) `DEMO_PREFIXES=(` stays untouched; cell 3 drives it unchanged.

## The exact change - TWO edits in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-demo-mutation.sh`

**Every line inside both fences carries a leading `+` or a leading `-`; there is no context line
anywhere in either fence.** The context each hunk needs is named here in prose and must be copied
VERBATIM from `files[...]`, never retyped from this brief. Every `+` line is plain ASCII: no em dash, no
backslash, no escape sequence, no dollar sign.

E1 - line 50. The line ABOVE it is line 49,
`# Determine the diff range. In CI this is the PR base..head; locally`, and the line BELOW it is line 51,
`if [ -n "${GITHUB_BASE_REF:-}" ]; then`. Both stay untouched.

```
-# default to comparing against origin/main.
+# default to comparing against origin/develop (KS-1033). The three-dot diff
+# below takes the merge-base, and under Git Flow develop is permanently ahead
+# of main, so an origin/main base shows the whole develop-vs-main delta as
+# this branch's own change - measured: 4 demo files on a branch that touched
+# nothing.
```

E2 - line 58. The line ABOVE it is line 57, `else`, and the line BELOW it is line 59, `  HEAD="HEAD"`.
Both stay untouched. Neither of those two context lines is unique on its own, but the hunk's span is,
because the `-` line is: `BASE="origin/main"` occurs on line 58 and nowhere else in the file.

```
-  BASE="origin/main"
+  BASE="origin/develop"
```

That is 2 removed lines and 6 added lines across two hunks. The `+` line in E2 keeps the original two
leading spaces.

Touch nothing else in the file. Do not edit `run-code-guards.sh`. Do not edit `preflight.sh`. Do not move
the guard out of the `DEFERRED` bucket. Do not add an environment-variable override for the base - the
two overrides that exist (`GITHUB_BASE_REF` and `$1`) are enough and both are already tested below.

## The test - CREATE THE NEW FILE `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_no_demo_mutation_base.test.sh`

File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_no_demo_mutation_base.test.sh`

### READ THIS BEFORE YOU WRITE THE FILE

- **The file below is 104 lines. Emit all 104 of them, verbatim, in the `+++ b/...` section of your diff.**
- There is no length constraint. Do not summarise, do not abbreviate, do not write a placeholder comment,
  do not write "the complete file should be created with the content from the brief", do not emit only
  the first line, and do not refer the reader back to this brief. The diff IS the deliverable.
- The body is plain ASCII, contains **no backslash anywhere**, and every construct in it is bash 3.2
  (macOS): no `mapfile`, no `declare -A`, no `${var,,}`, no `timeout`.
- If you find yourself about to write a sentence instead of shell, stop and write the shell.

### Where the shape comes from

Copy the shape - shebang, `set -uo pipefail`, the `export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null
GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null` line at FILE scope, `HERE` from `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}`, the
`SUBJ="${DEMO_GUARD_SH:-...}"` override, the readable-guard FATAL, the `mktemp -d` scratch tree +
`trap`, the bare-origin-plus-clone fixture, the `PASS`/`FAIL` counters and the summary + exit - from
`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh`, whose full content is in `files[...]`.
Like that suite, this one builds throwaway git repositories under `mktemp -d` and pushes only to a LOCAL
BARE REMOTE: nothing here reaches GitHub, and the repository's own files are never read or written. The
`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` export is not decoration - it is KS-883's fix, and without it an operator
with `commit.gpgsign = true` gets false reds from every cell.

**Reproduce the body below EXACTLY as written.** Do not invent a helper function, do not rename a
variable, do not describe the checks in your own shell - these are the literal cells, and each one either
increments `PASS` or increments `FAIL`. Every declaration the cells read (`EXPECTED_CELLS`, `DEMO_FILE`,
`PLAIN_FILE`, `RC_PLAIN`, `RC_DEMO`, `RC_CIREF` and the three output paths) is made ABOVE the first cell.

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-demo-mutation.sh - the DEFAULT diff
# base must be origin/develop, not origin/main (KS-1033 item 1)
# =============================================================================
# Under Git Flow develop is permanently ahead of main, so an origin/main base
# shows the whole develop-vs-main delta as this branch's own change. Every
# fixture is a throwaway repo under mktemp -d pushing to a LOCAL BARE REMOTE.
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_no_demo_mutation_base.test.sh
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SUBJ="${DEMO_GUARD_SH:-$HERE/../check-no-demo-mutation.sh}"
[ -r "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: check-no-demo-mutation.sh not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1033.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
PASS=0
FAIL=0
EXPECTED_CELLS=4
DEMO_FILE="Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql"
PLAIN_FILE="Blockchain/Dev/README.md"

build() {
  rm -rf "$1"
  mkdir -p "$1"
  (
    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null
    git init -q --bare -b main "$1/origin.git"
    git init -q -b main "$1/seed"
    cd "$1/seed" || exit 9
    git config user.email t@t.t
    git config user.name t
    mkdir -p Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/migrate
    echo base > "$PLAIN_FILE"
    echo base > "$DEMO_FILE"
    git add -A
    git commit -qm init
    git checkout -q -b develop
    echo "develop moved ahead" > "$DEMO_FILE"
    git add -A
    git commit -qm "develop touches a demo path"
    git remote add origin "$1/origin.git"
    git push -q origin main develop
    cd "$1" || exit 9
    git clone -q "$1/origin.git" work
    cd "$1/work" || exit 9
    git config user.email t@t.t
    git config user.name t
    git checkout -q -b feature origin/develop
    if [ "$2" = demo ]; then
      echo "feature touches a demo path too" > "$DEMO_FILE"
    else
      echo "an ordinary change" > "$PLAIN_FILE"
    fi
    git add -A
    git commit -qm "feature work"
  ) > "$1/build.log" 2>&1
}

run_guard() {
  (
    unset GITHUB_BASE_REF
    if [ -n "$2" ]; then export GITHUB_BASE_REF="$2"; fi
    cd "$1/work" || exit 9
    bash "$SUBJ"
  ) > "$1/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}

build "$WORK/plain" plain
RC_PLAIN="$(run_guard "$WORK/plain" "")"
OUT_PLAIN="$WORK/plain/out.txt"
build "$WORK/demo" demo
RC_DEMO="$(run_guard "$WORK/demo" "")"
OUT_DEMO="$WORK/demo/out.txt"
build "$WORK/ciref" plain
RC_CIREF="$(run_guard "$WORK/ciref" develop)"
OUT_CIREF="$WORK/ciref/out.txt"

# CELL 1 (RED at the tip) - a develop-based branch that touched no demo path
# must be allowed. At the tip the origin/main base drags develop's own demo
# commit into the diff and the guard exits 1.
if [ "$RC_PLAIN" = "0" ]; then
  echo "PASS: a develop-based branch touching no demo path exits 0"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: a develop-based branch touching no demo path exited $RC_PLAIN, not 0 - the base dragged in develop's own commits ($(grep -c 'migrate/init.sql' "$OUT_PLAIN") demo path line(s) reported)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 2 (RED at the tip) - and it must say so, not print the block banner.
if grep -qF 'no demo-shaping paths touched' "$OUT_PLAIN" && ! grep -qF 'DEMO MUTATION DETECTED' "$OUT_PLAIN"; then
  echo "PASS: the guard reports no demo-shaping paths touched and prints no block banner"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: clean-message present=$(grep -qF 'no demo-shaping paths touched' "$OUT_PLAIN" && echo yes || echo NO), block banner present=$(grep -qF 'DEMO MUTATION DETECTED' "$OUT_PLAIN" && echo YES || echo no)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 3 (GREEN CONTROL, tip AND after) - the guard still refuses a REAL demo
# change on the branch itself. This is what stops a fix that just always passes.
if [ "$RC_DEMO" = "1" ] && grep -qF 'DEMO MUTATION DETECTED' "$OUT_DEMO"; then
  echo "PASS: CONTROL a branch that really touches a demo path is still blocked with exit 1"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: CONTROL a real demo change exited $RC_DEMO (want 1), banner present=$(grep -qF 'DEMO MUTATION DETECTED' "$OUT_DEMO" && echo yes || echo NO)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 4 (GREEN CONTROL, tip AND after) - GITHUB_BASE_REF still wins over the
# default, so the branch named there is what the diff is taken against.
if [ "$RC_CIREF" = "0" ] && grep -qF 'no demo-shaping paths touched' "$OUT_CIREF"; then
  echo "PASS: CONTROL GITHUB_BASE_REF=develop is still honoured ahead of the default"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: CONTROL GITHUB_BASE_REF=develop exited $RC_CIREF (want 0): $(head -1 "$OUT_CIREF")"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 5 - the completeness guard. A suite that exits 0 having asserted nothing
# is a check that cannot fail, so a short count is itself a FAIL.
if [ $((PASS + FAIL)) -eq "$EXPECTED_CELLS" ]; then
  echo "PASS: all $EXPECTED_CELLS cells ran"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: only $((PASS + FAIL)) of $EXPECTED_CELLS cells ran - a suite that asserts nothing is not a pass"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

echo ""
echo "check_no_demo_mutation_base: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]
```

## Red cells

- 🔴 CELL 1 - a develop-based branch touching no demo path exits 0
- 🔴 CELL 2 - the guard reports no demo-shaping paths touched and prints no block banner

Cells 1 and 2 are the RED ones and both fail at the untouched tip **by assertion**, never by a crash. At
the tip the default base is `origin/main`; the merge-base of `origin/main` and `feature` is the initial
commit, so `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` contains develop's own
`Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql` change as well as the branch's `README.md` change. The
demo prefix matches, no commit in the range carries `[demo-mutation-allowed]`, and the guard exits 1
after printing the banner - so cell 1 reports `exited 1, not 0` and cell 2 reports the banner present and
the clean message absent. After the edit the base is `origin/develop`, whose merge-base with `feature` IS
the branch point, so the diff is the single `README.md` change and the guard prints
`[demo-guard] no demo-shaping paths touched` and exits 0.

Cells 3 and 4 are the GREEN CONTROLS and pass at the tip AND after. Cell 3 is the one that matters: a
branch that really edits `migrate/init.sql` is refused under BOTH bases (at the tip because develop's
change and the branch's change both match; after the edit because the branch's change matches), so a
"fix" that simply neutered the guard would redden it. Cell 4 pins the override that already worked -
`GITHUB_BASE_REF` is read at `:51-52` before the fallback is reached, so it is `origin/develop` on both
trees. Cell 5 is the COMPLETENESS GUARD: it asserts that `EXPECTED_CELLS` cells actually ran, so a suite
that drops its cells reports `0 passed, 1 failed` and rc 1 instead of a clean exit 0.

## Output

Exactly ONE ```diff block containing EXACTLY TWO files: the script
(`--- a/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-demo-mutation.sh` / `+++ b/...`, TWO hunks with correct counts,
context copied byte-for-byte from `files[...]`) and the new test
(`--- /dev/null` with NO leading space, then `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_no_demo_mutation_base.test.sh`).
No third file. No hunk for `run-code-guards.sh`.

## Notes for the raise (not for the model)

- **Measured at `48e65c435`, not eyeballed.** `git show 48e65c435:Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-demo-mutation.sh`
  piped into python: the file is 141 lines; line 58 is `'  BASE="origin/main"'` by exact string equality
  and that exact line occurs **once**; the substring `BASE="origin/main"` occurs on line 58 only; the
  substring `origin/main` occurs on lines 50 and 58 only; `origin/develop` occurs **zero** times in the
  file; line 50 is `'# default to comparing against origin/main.'` and occurs once. The failure banner
  text `DEMO MUTATION DETECTED` is at `:110` and the clean message
  `[demo-guard] no demo-shaping paths touched` at `:92`; the guard's refusal is `exit 1` at `:140`.
- **B6 is clear.** `git grep -l -F "check-no-demo-mutation" 48e65c435 -- Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__ systemTest/__tests__`
  returns NOTHING: no existing suite drives this guard, so there is no sibling to regress. The only three
  references anywhere in the tree are `run-code-guards.sh:116` (the DEFERRED reason), `preflight.sh:658`
  (leg 15's prose restating it) and `BACKLOG.md:50` - none of them a test, none of them asserted on.
- **The DEFERRED reason goes stale and that is deliberate.** `run-code-guards.sh:116` says *"it defaults
  to BASE=origin/main (line 58)"*. After this change that sentence is wrong. It is NOT edited here
  because the reason string is live bash inside an array (the file warns about that at `:108-113`) and
  because editing it is one keystroke from wiring the guard, which is a separate call. **The PR
  description must say so**, and the follow-up is "wire it or rewrite its DEFERRED reason" - a decision
  with a measured push behind it, not a rider on this diff.
- **Why `origin/develop` and not a literal `git merge-base` call.** `:69` already uses the three-dot
  form, which IS the merge-base. The ticket's words are "base it on the merge-base with `origin/develop`";
  with `BASE="origin/develop"` the existing `"$BASE...$HEAD"` resolves to exactly that. Adding an explicit
  `git merge-base` invocation would add a second failure mode (a base that does not resolve) that `:63-66`
  already handles for the ref form.
- **The fresh-clone case still exits 0.** `:63-66` verifies the base and prints
  `base origin/develop not found; nothing to compare` on a tree that has no `origin/develop`, exactly as
  it did for `origin/main`. This change cannot make the guard harder to run.
- **What this deliberately does NOT do.** It does not wire the guard, does not touch
  `check-no-trust-header-reads.sh` (KS-1033 item 2, decision-class by the ticket's own words), does not
  touch `check-container-isolation.sh` (item 3, a relocation), and does not change `:98`'s two-dot
  `git log "$BASE..$HEAD"` override-token scan - that asymmetry with `:69`'s three dots is real but is
  not KS-1033's, and folding it in would put an unticketed change in this diff.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# DEMO-MUTATION GUARD (2026-04-28 demo-isolation lockdown)
# =============================================================================
# Refuses any commit that touches files known to shape the live demo
# environment, unless the commit message contains the explicit override
# token `[demo-mutation-allowed]`.
#
# Why this exists: the demo Azure environment (resource group
# secuura-demo-rg) is in active customer use during the connector-
# overhaul sprint. We disabled auto-deploy from main + develop in this
# commit, but a future engineer might re-enable it OR a config edit
# could shape the live env via secrets / Bicep templates without going
# through deploy. This guard is the second line of defence: PR review
# fails if the diff touches a demo-shaping path.
#
# Wired into:
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml (build job, between lints and build)
#   - Pre-commit hook (optional, if developer wants local enforcement)
#
# To override (deliberate demo change):
#   git commit -m "Update demo config [demo-mutation-allowed]
#
#   Why: <explicit reason>"
#
# This is INTENTIONALLY noisy — false-positives are cheaper than
# accidentally shipping to live customers.
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# Paths that shape the live demo environment. Touching ANY of these
# requires the override token.
DEMO_PATHS=(
  "Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/env.demo.json"
  # NOTE (KS-318): the old Blockchain/Dev/.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml
  # guard entry was dropped — that stale workflow dir was removed (GitHub only
  # runs the repo-root .github/workflows/). The live demo deploy is the
  # repo-root deploy-demo.yml; guarding it is a separate follow-up.
)

# Path PREFIXES that shape the demo environment. Anything under these
# trees is also gated.
DEMO_PREFIXES=(
  "Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/migrate/"
  # Bicep templates that drive the demo RG resources
)

# Determine the diff range. In CI this is the PR base..head; locally
# default to comparing against origin/main.
if [ -n "${GITHUB_BASE_REF:-}" ]; then
  BASE="origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}"
  HEAD="HEAD"
elif [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then
  BASE="$1"
  HEAD="${2:-HEAD}"
else
  BASE="origin/main"
  HEAD="HEAD"
fi

# Skip if we can't resolve the base (first commit on a fresh clone).
if ! git rev-parse --verify "$BASE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[demo-guard] base $BASE not found; nothing to compare"
  exit 0
fi

# Files changed in this diff
CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE...$HEAD" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -z "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
  echo "[demo-guard] no files changed; nothing to check"
  exit 0
fi

# Find any demo-mutating change
MUTATIONS=()
while IFS= read -r f; do
  for p in "${DEMO_PATHS[@]}"; do
    if [ "$f" = "$p" ]; then
      MUTATIONS+=("$f")
      continue 2
    fi
  done
  for prefix in "${DEMO_PREFIXES[@]}"; do
    case "$f" in
      "$prefix"*) MUTATIONS+=("$f"); continue 2 ;;
    esac
  done
done <<< "$CHANGED_FILES"

if [ ${#MUTATIONS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo-guard] no demo-shaping paths touched"
  exit 0
fi

# Demo path touched — check for the override token in any commit message
# in this diff range.
COMMIT_MSGS=$(git log "$BASE..$HEAD" --pretty=%B 2>/dev/null || true)
if echo "$COMMIT_MSGS" | grep -qF "[demo-mutation-allowed]"; then
  echo "[demo-guard] demo paths touched but override token present — allowed"
  echo "  paths:"
  printf '    %s\n' "${MUTATIONS[@]}"
  exit 0
fi

# No override → fail loudly
cat <<EOF >&2

╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                  DEMO MUTATION DETECTED — BLOCKED                  ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

This change touches files known to shape the live demo environment:

EOF

printf '    %s\n' "${MUTATIONS[@]}" >&2

cat <<EOF >&2

The live demo (Azure RG secuura-demo-rg) is in active customer use
during the connector-overhaul sprint. We don't want unintended config
shifts.

If this change is INTENTIONAL (deliberate demo update), add this
override token to ANY commit in the PR:

    [demo-mutation-allowed]

Example:
    git commit -m "Update demo env config [demo-mutation-allowed]

    Why: <explicit reason — what it does, who approved>"

If this change is unintentional, revert the demo-touching files
(or move them to a follow-up PR) and try again.

EOF

exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for .githooks/pre-push — base resolution (KS-854)
# =============================================================================
# The defect this exists for: on a FRESH CLONE the gate skipped entirely and
# said nothing.
#
# `git clone` creates only the default branch locally, so `develop` exists
# solely as `refs/remotes/origin/develop`. The hook did a bare
# `git merge-base develop HEAD` into a `$(…)` with stderr discarded; that
# failed, `base` was empty, `changed` stayed empty, and
# `[ -z "$changed" ] && exit 0` returned SUCCESS before leg 1. Push rc 0, in
# seconds, with no `[pre-push]` line at all — no gate, and no signal there was
# no gate. Reported as F-850-02 by the #840 gate, which hit it by accident.
#
# It is the same shape as KS-676 (a CVE scan reporting clean having examined
# nothing) and KS-853 (leg 9 passing a planted violation): AN EMPTY RESULT READ
# AS A PASS. So the cases below assert on whether the hook ANNOUNCED ITSELF,
# not on the preflight's verdict — "did the gate run" is the property that was
# lost, and a suite that only checked exit codes would have passed throughout
# (the broken hook exits 0, and so does a healthy skip).
#
# Every fixture pushes to a LOCAL BARE REMOTE. Nothing here reaches GitHub.
# The preflight is stubbed to an instant `exit 0` on purpose: this suite tests
# the hook's DISPATCH, not the preflight's legs, and a real preflight would
# make the fixtures depend on node_modules and a running stack.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/pre_push_hook_base.test.sh
#        HOOK_SH=/path/to/other/pre-push bash …   (to test a different copy)
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

# KS-883 — ISOLATE THE GIT CONFIG FOR THE WHOLE FILE, NOT JUST THE FIXTURE BUILD.
#
# This export used to live inside `build_fixture`'s subshell, so it isolated the
# BUILD and nothing else: the CONTROL and CASES 1-3 ran under whatever global
# git config the operator has. Measured with `commit.gpgsign = true` and an
# unusable `gpg.program`, which is an ordinary developer configuration:
#
#   hostile global config -> 4 passed, 2 failed   (CASE 1 falsely RED)
#   GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null -> 6 passed, 0 failed
#
# and the run printed `fatal: failed to write commit object` twice. CASE 1 was
# red for a reason that has nothing to do with the hook, and CASE 2's `ok` was
# VACUOUS in the same run — its commit failed too, so the push it asserts on
# carried no docs change at all. A green cell there meant nothing.
#
# Leg 12 of the preflight now reaches this suite on every gated push, so anyone
# who signs their commits gets that red, pointing at the hook rather than at
# their own config.
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
HOOK="${HOOK_SH:-$REPO_ROOT/.githooks/pre-push}"

if [[ ! -f "$HOOK" ]]; then
  echo "FATAL: pre-push hook not found at $HOOK" >&2
  exit 2
fi

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks854.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0
fail=0

ok()   { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad()  { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# Build a fixture repo. $1 = dir, $2 = "with-develop" | "no-develop".
# Leaves you with: a bare origin, and a clone whose ONLY local branch is main.
build_fixture() {
  local root="$1" mode="$2"
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root"
  (
    # Inherited from file scope (KS-883); repeated here so the fixture stays
    # hermetic if this function is ever lifted into another suite.
    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null
    git init -q --bare -b main "$root/origin.git"
    git init -q -b main "$root/seed"
    cd "$root/seed"
    git config user.email t@t.t; git config user.name t
    mkdir -p Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight systemTest docs
    echo base > Blockchain/Dev/file.txt
    echo docs > docs/readme.md
    printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho "[preflight] ran"\nexit 0\n' \
      > Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh
    : > systemTest/slot-target.sh
    # KS-989: the hook now invokes the systemTest formatting gate, so the fixture
    # must provide one — the same reason preflight.sh is stubbed above. A STUB,
    # not the real script: this suite is about base resolution, and the real gate
    # has its own suite (systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh).
    # It records that it was invoked (CASE 7) and fails on demand (CASE 8).
    mkdir -p systemTest/scripts
    cat > systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh <<'GATE_STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"
{ printf 'argv=%s\n' "$*"; [ "${1:-}" = "--all" ] || cat; } > "$root/.gate-invoked" 2>/dev/null
[ -f "$root/.gate-should-fail" ] && { echo "[format-gate] stub refusing on demand" >&2; exit 1; }
exit 0
GATE_STUB
    chmod +x systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh
    git add -A; git commit -qm init
    if [ "$mode" = with-develop ]; then
      git branch develop
    fi
    git remote add origin "$root/origin.git"
    if [ "$mode" = with-develop ]; then
      git push -q origin main develop
    else
      git push -q origin main
    fi
    cd "$root"
    git clone -q "$root/origin.git" fresh
    cd fresh
    git config user.email t@t.t; git config user.name t
    mkdir -p .githooks
    cp "$HOOK" .githooks/pre-push
    chmod +x .githooks/pre-push
    git config core.hooksPath .githooks
  ) >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONTROL FIRST — the fixture really does reproduce the fresh-clone shape.
# Without this, every case below could be passing for the wrong reason.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c0" with-develop
(
  cd "$WORK/c0/fresh"
  branches="$(git branch --format='%(refname:short)' | tr '\n' ' ')"
  git rev-parse --verify develop >/dev/null 2>&1 && local_dev=YES || local_dev=NO
  git rev-parse --verify origin/develop >/dev/null 2>&1 && remote_dev=YES || remote_dev=NO
  # KS-881: cut the branch the CASES cut, and report ITS upstream. The fixture's
  # shape is not only "no local develop" — it is also "the branch under test has
  # no upstream", and that half was invisible in this line.
  git checkout -q -b feature/x --no-track origin/develop
  up="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref 'feature/x@{upstream}' 2>/dev/null)"
  [ -n "$up" ] || up=NONE
  printf '%s|%s|%s|%s\n' "$branches" "$local_dev" "$remote_dev" "$up"
) > "$WORK/c0.out" 2>/dev/null
IFS='|' read -r c0_branches c0_local c0_remote c0_up < "$WORK/c0.out"
if [ "$c0_local" = NO ] && [ "$c0_remote" = YES ] && [ "$c0_up" = NONE ]; then
  ok "CONTROL — the fixture is a real fresh clone: local branches [${c0_branches% }], develop local=NO remote=YES, upstream=NONE"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the fixture is a real fresh clone" \
      "expected local develop NO + origin/develop YES + upstream NONE; got local=$c0_local remote=$c0_remote upstream=$c0_up"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 1 — THE REGRESSION. Fresh clone, no local develop, branch with NO
# upstream, carrying a real Blockchain/Dev change. The gate MUST announce.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c1" with-develop
out1="$(
  cd "$WORK/c1/fresh"
  git checkout -q -b feature/x --no-track origin/develop
  # KS-881 — ASSERT THE PRECONDITION THIS CASE RESTS ON.
  #
  # `--no-track` is what makes this branch have NO upstream, which is what sends
  # the hook down the base-resolution path under test. Nothing asserted it.
  # Measured: drop `--no-track` and the branch tracks origin/develop, `changed`
  # comes from `@{upstream}` instead, the gate runs for an unrelated reason, and
  # the suite goes 2/4 -> 4/2 AT THE PARENT HOOK — this case passes against the
  # very bug it exists for, and the CONTROL cannot see the loss.
  if git rev-parse --abbrev-ref 'feature/x@{upstream}' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: feature/x has an upstream; --no-track is not in effect"
  fi
  echo change > Blockchain/Dev/file.txt
  git add -A; git commit -qm "a Blockchain/Dev change"
  # KS-883 — the commit must have LANDED, or everything below asserts on a push
  # that carried nothing. A signing failure is silent to a grep of push output.
  git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q 'a Blockchain/Dev change' || echo "COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND"
  git push origin feature/x 2>&1
)"
if printf '%s' "$out1" | grep -q '\[pre-push\]'; then
  ok "fresh clone + no upstream + a Blockchain/Dev change → the gate RUNS and says so"
else
  bad "fresh clone + no upstream + a Blockchain/Dev change → the gate RUNS and says so" \
      "no [pre-push] line: the gate skipped silently (KS-854)"
fi

# KS-881 — the precondition really was absent, ASSERTED rather than assumed.
if printf '%s' "$out1" | grep -q 'PRECONDITION-LOST'; then
  bad "CASE 1's branch really has no upstream (the --no-track precondition holds)" \
      "feature/x tracks a remote branch, so this case exercises the @{upstream} path, not the base-resolution path it exists for"
else
  ok "CASE 1's branch really has no upstream — the precondition is asserted, not assumed"
fi

# The preflight really was invoked — otherwise case 1 proves nothing.
if printf '%s' "$out1" | grep -q '\[preflight\] ran'; then
  ok "…and the preflight was actually invoked, not merely announced"
else
  bad "…and the preflight was actually invoked, not merely announced" \
      "the [pre-push] line appeared but the preflight never ran"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 2 — the fix must not become "always run". A docs-only push still skips.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c2" with-develop
out2="$(
  cd "$WORK/c2/fresh"
  git checkout -q -b docs/x --no-track origin/develop
  echo more >> docs/readme.md
  git add -A; git commit -qm "docs only"
  # KS-883 — without this, a failed commit makes this case pass VACUOUSLY: the

  git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q 'docs only' || echo "COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND"

if printf '%s' "$out2" | grep -q '\[pre-push\]'; then

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 3 — nothing resolves at all (no develop, no origin/develop, no

build_fixture "$WORK/c3" no-develop
out3="$(

  echo change > Blockchain/Dev/file.txt

if printf '%s' "$out3" | grep -q 'KS-854'; then

else

      "no KS-854 line; an uncomputable base was treated as a clean tree"
fi
if printf '%s' "$out3" | grep -q '\[preflight\] ran'; then

else

fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 4 — KS-882. The gate must not trust the FIRST ref that resolves.
#
# A local `develop` that already contains the branch tip makes
# `git merge-base develop HEAD` return HEAD, the diff empty, and the hook exit 0
# in silence — while `origin/develop` still holds the old content, so a real
# Blockchain/Dev change goes up UNGATED. Measured against the parent hook:
# push rc 0, zero `[pre-push]` lines, preflight never invoked, and the bare
# origin afterwards reading feature/x = change, develop = base.
#
# The preconditions are asserted, not assumed (KS-881's lesson): this case only
# tests what it is named for if local develop CONTAINS head while origin/develop
# does NOT.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c4" with-develop
out4="$(
  cd "$WORK/c4/fresh"
  git checkout -q -b feature/x --no-track origin/develop
  echo change > Blockchain/Dev/file.txt
  git add -A; git commit -qm "a Blockchain/Dev change"
  git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q 'a Blockchain/Dev change' || echo "COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND"
  # THE ONE LINE THIS CASE IS ABOUT.
  git branch -f develop HEAD
  git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD develop 2>/dev/null \
    || echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: local develop does not contain HEAD"
  git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/develop 2>/dev/null \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: origin/develop already contains HEAD, so nothing is ungated"
  git rev-parse --abbrev-ref 'feature/x@{upstream}' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: feature/x has an upstream; the base-resolution path is not exercised"
  git push origin feature/x 2>&1
)"
if printf '%s' "$out4" | grep -q 'PRECONDITION-LOST'; then
  bad "CASE 4's preconditions hold (local develop contains HEAD, origin/develop does not, no upstream)" \
      "$(printf '%s' "$out4" | grep 'PRECONDITION-LOST' | tr '\n' ';')"
else
  ok "CASE 4's preconditions hold — local develop contains HEAD, origin/develop does not, branch has no upstream"
fi
if printf '%s' "$out4" | grep -q '\[pre-push\]'; then
  ok "a local develop containing the tip → the gate still RUNS and says so (KS-882)"
else
  bad "a local develop containing the tip → the gate still RUNS and says so (KS-882)" \
      "no [pre-push] line: the hook trusted local develop, diffed HEAD against HEAD and skipped silently"
fi
if printf '%s' "$out4" | grep -q '\[preflight\] ran'; then
  ok "…and the preflight was actually invoked on that push, not merely announced"
else
  bad "…and the preflight was actually invoked on that push, not merely announced" \
      "the gate announced but the preflight never ran"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 5 — KS-882, the degenerate half. When EVERY resolvable ref contains
# HEAD, the empty diff carries no information at all: there is no ref left that
# can say what is new. Reordering the ref list cannot help here, which is why
# the fix is "ask them all, and treat all-bases-equal-HEAD as uncomputable"
# rather than "put origin/develop first".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c5" with-develop
out5="$(
  cd "$WORK/c5/fresh"
  git checkout -q -b feature/x --no-track origin/develop
  echo change > Blockchain/Dev/file.txt
  git add -A; git commit -qm "a Blockchain/Dev change"
  git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q 'a Blockchain/Dev change' || echo "COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND"
  git branch -f develop HEAD
  git update-ref -d refs/remotes/origin/develop
  git rev-parse --verify --quiet origin/develop >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: origin/develop still resolves, so a second ref is available"
  git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD develop 2>/dev/null \
    || echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: local develop does not contain HEAD"
  git push origin feature/x 2>&1
)"
if printf '%s' "$out5" | grep -q 'PRECONDITION-LOST'; then
  bad "CASE 5's preconditions hold (only local develop resolves, and it contains HEAD)" \
      "$(printf '%s' "$out5" | grep 'PRECONDITION-LOST' | tr '\n' ';')"
else
  ok "CASE 5's preconditions hold — only local develop resolves, and it contains HEAD"
fi
if printf '%s' "$out5" | grep -q 'KS-882'; then
  ok "every resolvable base equals HEAD → the hook says so LOUDLY"
else
  bad "every resolvable base equals HEAD → the hook says so LOUDLY" \
      "no KS-882 line; an uninformative base was read as a clean tree"
fi
if printf '%s' "$out5" | grep -q '\[preflight\] ran'; then
  ok "every resolvable base equals HEAD → the preflight RUNS anyway (fails safe)"
else
  bad "every resolvable base equals HEAD → the preflight RUNS anyway (fails safe)" \
      "the gate skipped when it had no informative base"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 6 — the KS-882 fix must not become "always run" either. The same local

build_fixture "$WORK/c6" with-develop
out6="$(
  cd "$WORK/c6/fresh"
  git checkout -q -b docs/y --no-track origin/develop
  echo more >> docs/readme.md
  git add -A; git commit -qm "docs only"

fi

build_fixture "$WORK/c7" with-develop
out7="$(

)"
if printf '%s' "$out7" | grep -q 'systemTest/akto/docs/quick_start.md'; then

else

fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 9 — KS-909. PROPERTY 1: the loop must ask EVERY resolvable ref, not stop
# at the first one that produces an INFORMATIVE base.
#
# #861 shipped two properties and guarded one. CASES 4-6 all pass against a hook
# that breaks at the first informative ref, so nothing held the `continue` that
# makes the loop keep asking — the suite stayed 16/0 under that tamper.
#
# The state that separates them: local `develop` AHEAD of `origin/develop` by a
# Blockchain/Dev change that has been merged locally and NOT pushed, with the
# branch cut from local develop and carrying a DOCS-ONLY commit on top.
#   merge-base(develop, HEAD)        -> informative, and its diff has NO Blockchain/Dev
#   merge-base(origin/develop, HEAD) -> informative, and its diff HAS the unpushed one
# A hook that stops at the first informative ref sees only the docs commit and
# skips SILENTLY, while the push really does carry a Blockchain/Dev change the
# remote has never seen. Same class as KS-882, one ref-selection rule further on.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c7" with-develop
out9="$(
  cd "$WORK/c7/fresh"
  # Local develop at the origin tip, then a Blockchain/Dev change committed on
  # it and deliberately NOT pushed. (No apostrophe in this comment on purpose:
  # inside a $( ) an apostrophe in a COMMENT is still an unterminated quote to
  # the parser, and the error it raises points at the substitution, not here.)
  # This is what makes local develop AHEAD of origin.
  git checkout -q -b develop --no-track origin/develop
  echo change > Blockchain/Dev/file.txt
  git add -A; git commit -qm "a Blockchain/Dev change merged locally, not pushed"
  git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q 'merged locally' || echo "COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND"
  # The branch under test: cut from LOCAL develop, docs only on top.
  git checkout -q -b feature/w --no-track develop
  echo more >> docs/readme.md
  git add -A; git commit -qm "docs only"
  git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q 'docs only' || echo "COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND"

  # PRECONDITIONS, asserted rather than assumed — all four, because any one of
  # them failing would let this case pass for the ordinary reason.
  git rev-parse --abbrev-ref 'feature/w@{upstream}' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: feature/w has an upstream; the base-resolution path is not exercised"
  head=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
  b_local=$(git merge-base develop HEAD)
  b_origin=$(git merge-base origin/develop HEAD)
  [ "$b_local" = "$head" ]  && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: the local-develop base is HEAD, so this is the KS-882 case, not this one"
  [ "$b_origin" = "$head" ] && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: the origin/develop base is HEAD, so this is the KS-882 case, not this one"
  git diff --name-only "$b_local"  HEAD | grep -q '^Blockchain/Dev/' \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: the local-develop diff already carries a Blockchain/Dev path, so the first ref alone would run the gate"
  git diff --name-only "$b_origin" HEAD | grep -q '^Blockchain/Dev/' \
    || echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: the origin/develop diff carries NO Blockchain/Dev path, so there is nothing for the second ref to find"

  git push origin feature/w 2>&1
)"
if printf '%s' "$out9" | grep -q 'PRECONDITION-LOST'; then
  bad "CASE 9's preconditions hold (both bases informative; only origin's diff carries Blockchain/Dev)" \
      "$(printf '%s' "$out9" | grep 'PRECONDITION-LOST' | tr '\n' ';')"
else
  ok "CASE 9's preconditions hold — both bases informative, and ONLY origin/develop's diff carries a Blockchain/Dev path"
fi
if printf '%s' "$out9" | grep -q '\[pre-push\]'; then
  ok "the loop asks EVERY ref — a second, further base finds the change the first missed (KS-909)"
else
  bad "the loop asks EVERY ref — a second, further base finds the change the first missed (KS-909)" \
      "no [pre-push] line: the hook stopped at the first informative ref and skipped silently, while the push carried an unpushed Blockchain/Dev change"
fi
if printf '%s' "$out9" | grep -q '\[preflight\] ran'; then
  ok "…and the preflight was actually invoked on that push, not merely announced"
else
  bad "…and the preflight was actually invoked on that push, not merely announced" \
      "the gate announced but the preflight never ran"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 10 — KS-991. A STALE local `develop` must not INVENT a change.
#
# Local `develop` is a strict ancestor of `origin/develop`: the trunk moved by
# a commit that touches Blockchain/Dev and the operator never refreshed the
# local ref. The branch is cut from `origin/develop` with `--no-track` and
# carries a DOCS-ONLY commit. Diffed against the stale ref the branch appears
# to carry the trunk's Blockchain/Dev change; diffed against origin/develop it
# carries nothing of the kind. Measured 2026-09-08, three pushes in one
# session: the hook took the stale base, ran the full preflight on a branch
# touching no Blockchain/Dev file, and one run then failed on an environment
# condition presented as a gate result. A ref BEHIND the remote can only
# inflate the diff (its diff is a superset of the better ref's) — it cannot
# conceal anything — so the hook must ignore it, say so, and skip.
#
# The direction is the OPPOSITE of CASE 4: there a ref CONTAINING the tip hid
# a change; here a ref behind the remote invents one. CASE 11 is the control.
#
# The stale ref is advanced from the SEED clone, which has no hook, so the only
# hooked push in this fixture is the one under test. Preconditions asserted:
# local develop is a strict ancestor of origin/develop, the two differ, the gap
# carries a Blockchain/Dev path, the branch itself does not, no upstream.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c10" with-develop
out10="$(
  cd "$WORK/c10/fresh"
  # Local develop at the CURRENT origin tip first, so that once the seed has
  # advanced origin it sits one commit behind: a strict ancestor.
  git branch develop origin/develop
  # Advance origin/develop by a Blockchain/Dev change from the seed (no hook).
  (
    cd "$WORK/c10/seed"
    git checkout -q develop
    echo trunk-moved > Blockchain/Dev/trunk.txt
    git add -A; git commit -qm "a Blockchain/Dev change on the trunk, not yet in local develop"
    git push -q origin develop
  ) >/dev/null 2>&1
  git fetch -q origin
  # The branch under test: cut from origin/develop, docs only on top.
  git checkout -q -b docs/stale --no-track origin/develop
  echo more >> docs/readme.md
  git add -A; git commit -qm "docs only"
  git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q 'docs only' || echo "COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND"

  # PRECONDITIONS, asserted rather than assumed — any one of them failing
  # would let this case pass or fail for a reason that is not the stale ref.
  git rev-parse --abbrev-ref 'docs/stale@{upstream}' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: docs/stale has an upstream; the base-resolution path is not exercised"
  git merge-base --is-ancestor develop origin/develop 2>/dev/null \
    || echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: local develop is not an ancestor of origin/develop, so the stale-ref rule cannot apply"
  [ "$(git rev-parse develop)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/develop)" ] \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: local develop equals origin/develop, so it is current, not stale"
  git diff --name-only develop origin/develop | grep -q '^Blockchain/Dev/' \
    || echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: the gap between local develop and origin/develop carries no Blockchain/Dev path, so a stale base could not inflate the diff"
  git diff --name-only origin/develop HEAD | grep -q '^Blockchain/Dev/' \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: the branch itself carries a Blockchain/Dev path, so the gate would run for the ordinary reason"

  git push origin docs/stale 2>&1
)"
if printf '%s' "$out10" | grep -q 'PRECONDITION-LOST'; then
  bad "CASE 10's preconditions hold (local develop a strict ancestor of origin/develop; the gap carries Blockchain/Dev; the branch does not; no upstream)" \
      "$(printf '%s' "$out10" | grep 'PRECONDITION-LOST' | tr '\n' ';')"
else
  ok "CASE 10's preconditions hold — local develop is a strict ancestor of origin/develop, the gap carries a Blockchain/Dev path, the branch does not, and it has no upstream"
fi
if printf '%s' "$out10" | grep -q 'KS-991'; then
  ok "CASE 10 — a stale local develop is IGNORED for base selection, and the hook says so (KS-991)"
else
  bad "CASE 10 — a stale local develop is IGNORED for base selection, and the hook says so (KS-991)" \
      "no KS-991 line: the stale ref was consulted silently"
fi
if printf '%s' "$out10" | grep -q '\[preflight\] ran'; then
  bad "CASE 10 — a docs-only push on a CURRENT base SKIPS the preflight" \
      "the preflight ran: the stale local develop inflated the diff with the trunk's Blockchain/Dev change (the KS-991 defect)"
else
  ok "CASE 10 — a docs-only push on a CURRENT base SKIPS the preflight, despite the stale local develop"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CASE 11 — the KS-991 fix must not become "always skip". The SAME stale local
# develop, but the branch DOES touch a Blockchain/Dev file: origin/develop is
# still consulted, its diff shows the file, and the gate RUNS. Without this
# cell a fix that skipped whenever local develop was stale would pass CASE 10
# and be wrong in exactly the way CASE 2 and CASE 6 exist to prevent.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/c11" with-develop
out11="$(
  cd "$WORK/c11/fresh"
  git branch develop origin/develop
  (
    cd "$WORK/c11/seed"
    git checkout -q develop
    echo trunk-moved > Blockchain/Dev/trunk.txt
    git add -A; git commit -qm "a Blockchain/Dev change on the trunk, not yet in local develop"
    git push -q origin develop
  ) >/dev/null 2>&1
  git fetch -q origin
  git checkout -q -b feature/stale --no-track origin/develop
  echo change > Blockchain/Dev/file.txt
  git add -A; git commit -qm "a Blockchain/Dev change"
  git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q 'a Blockchain/Dev change' || echo "COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND"
  git rev-parse --abbrev-ref 'feature/stale@{upstream}' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: feature/stale has an upstream; the base-resolution path is not exercised"
  git merge-base --is-ancestor develop origin/develop 2>/dev/null \
    || echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: local develop is not an ancestor of origin/develop, so the stale-ref rule cannot apply"
  [ "$(git rev-parse develop)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/develop)" ] \
    && echo "PRECONDITION-LOST: local develop equals origin/develop, so it is current, not stale"
  git push origin feature/stale 2>&1
)"
if printf '%s' "$out11" | grep -q 'PRECONDITION-LOST'; then
  bad "CASE 11's preconditions hold (the same stale local develop; no upstream)" \
      "$(printf '%s' "$out11" | grep 'PRECONDITION-LOST' | tr '\n' ';')"
else
  ok "CASE 11's preconditions hold — the same stale local develop, and the branch has no upstream"
fi
if printf '%s' "$out11" | grep -q '\[preflight\] ran'; then
  ok "CASE 11 — a real Blockchain/Dev change on the branch still RUNS the preflight with a stale local develop (the fix did not become 'always skip')"
else
  bad "CASE 11 — a real Blockchain/Dev change on the branch still RUNS the preflight with a stale local develop" \
      "the preflight did not run: ignoring the stale ref dropped the gate — the KS-991 fix became 'always skip'"
fi

# KS-883 — every case's commit must have LANDED. A signing failure is invisible
# to a grep of push output, and turns CASE 1 falsely red and CASE 2 vacuously
# green in the same run.
landed=0
for out_name in out1 out2 out3 out4 out5 out6 out7 out8 out9 out10 out11; do
  eval "out_val=\$$out_name"
  if printf '%s' "$out_val" | grep -q 'COMMIT-DID-NOT-LAND'; then
    bad "every case's commit landed before its push ($out_name)" \
        "the commit failed, so the push asserted on carried nothing — check commit.gpgsign and gpg.program"
    landed=1
  fi
done
[ "$landed" -eq 0 ] && ok "every case's commit LANDED before its push, so each assertion is on a real change"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
